messages:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — after rolling runtime v1.13 to the canary pool (~10% of traffic) at 09:03 UTC we started seeing p95 jump from ~220ms -> ~480ms and p99 spikes to ~1.2s. Affected route: /v1/generate (text-gen). Grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/latency.

AJ Park: seeing it too. Is this the new kernel-selector change (KSEL-57) or the quantization path tweak? I noticed a code change in the rollout: commit abcdef1 -> changed kernel selection priority.

Devon Li: quick metric snapshot from canary (09:00-09:20): p50 110ms, p95 480ms (+118%), p99 1200ms (+300%). Overall QPS steady. No error rate increase. Looks like tail latency only.

Carlos (SRE): @Maria can you pull a histogram and check seq-length buckets? Maybe long sequences hitting a slower kernel. Also check KV cache hit rate — if cache misses went up that could explain regen overhead.

Maria Chen: good idea. Histogram shows tail dominated by seq_len >= 1024 requests. KV cache hit rate dropped from 94% -> 65% on canary. Suspect new runtime path disables prefix caching for certain code paths.

Eve (Perf): I grabbed flame traces from a few p99 samples. The slow path is in kernel_dispatch -> quantized_matmul_fallback (lots of memcpy). Compare with baseline v1.12 where it went to quantized_matmul_opt. Looks like the kernel selector favored a fallback kernel for long sequences.

AJ Park: that aligns with the KSEL-57 change — it introduced a metric-based selector that weighted memory-pressure heuristics differently. Might be misclassifying for GPUs with bigger sequence profiles.

Maria Chen: Repro steps I ran locally against the canary endpoint (redwood-canary.example):
```bash
# simple hammer to reproduce tail latency
for i in {1..200}; do 
  curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST \ 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-13b","input":"'$(python -c 'print("x"*1200)')'"}' \ 
    https://redwood-canary.example/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
This reliably increases observed p95 to ~480ms after warmup.

Carlos (SRE): Thanks — can you also run with header `X-Redwood-Debug: full` to capture kernel selection logs? We'll need kernel IDs.

Maria Chen: added logs. Kernel selection lines: `kernel_selector: chose kernel_id=K_QUANT_FALLBACK for seq_len=1200, reason=memory_budget_estimate`. Baseline (v1.12) had `kernel_id=K_QUANT_OPT`.

Devon Li: OK. Immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback canary to v1.12 (fast) 2) patch kernel-selector weighting and redeploy to canary (slower) 3) add a temporary rule to force kernel_id=K_QUANT_OPT for seq_len >= 1024. Thoughts?

Eve (Perf): For minimal blast radius, I'd prefer 1) rollback to restore tail latencies, and 2) create a targeted hotfix for selector rules to test in a separate canary pool. Forcing kernel via rule is safe as short-term but we should avoid long-term overrides.

AJ Park: I'm +1 for rollback. Not willing to degrade enterprise SLAs for a selector tuning bug. Maria — can you trigger rollback and then collect post-rollback metrics?

Maria Chen: rolling back canary to v1.12 now. @deploy-bot please start rollback.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Initiating rollback of runtime v1.13 -> v1.12 for canary pool. Rollback ID: rb-20260315-001. Starting ...

Carlos (SRE): I'll watch the canary dashboards and verify KV cache hit rate and p95.

Maria Chen: rollback completed at 09:26 UTC per deploy-bot.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Rollback rb-20260315-001 completed. Health checks passed.

Devon Li: post-rollback snapshot (09:30-09:40): p95 back to 225ms, p99 ~260ms, KV cache hit rate returned to 93%. Looks like rollback fixed it.

Eve (Perf): Saved flame traces for one of the earlier bad samples and one post-rollback sample. Post-rollback shows kernel_dispatch -> quantized_matmul_opt (fast) as expected. Created perf ticket: PERF-412 to track root cause.

AJ Park: Next steps:
- PERF-412: bisect KSEL-57 changes (unit tests + perf harness) to find exact offending line.
- Add automated perf-sanity check in canary pipeline: after each runtime rollout run a small seq_len=1200 workload and assert p95 delta < 20%.
- Temporary: add a canary-only protection that pins kernel-selector to v1.12 rules until selector fix lands.

Carlos (SRE): Also file an incident postmortem with timeline and impact (customer complaints? none escalated yet, we got internal alerts). I'll create INCIDENT-20260315-09.

Maria Chen: I'll attach debug logs and the reproducer script to PERF-412 and INCIDENT-20260315-09.

Devon Li: For the bisect plan: use git bisect on the runtime repo between tags v1.12 and v1.13 with the perf harness that runs 200 requests at seq_len=1200 and measures p95. I have a small script to automate; pushing to tools/perf/bisect-runner.

Eve (Perf): note: keep GPU type constant when bisecting (we saw selector behavior change by GPU model). Use the same instance type as canary (g4dn-16xlarge in us-west-2).

AJ Park: Good call. Also check driver/roc/ CUDA versions; kernel heuristics rely on driver mem reporting. Add driver version to canary telemetry.

Maria Chen: closing the immediate incident since rollback resolved latency. Summary in INCIDENT-20260315-09: runtime v1.13 introduced a kernel-selector heuristic that favored fallback kernel for long sequences leading to increased p95/p99. Mitigation: rolled back to v1.12, follow-ups: PERF-412 (bisect & fix), add canary perf-sanity check, telemetry improvements.

Carlos (SRE): marking paging watchlist for next rollout. If anyone sees tail reappear please escalate to #incidents.

AJ Park: Great response team. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Maria Chen: thanks — I'll keep updates on PERF-412.
